correctness.rationale: An exactly specified 11-vertex graph and tie-retaining update yield a finite 2048-state map. Exhaustive standard-library functional-graph decomposition and an independently coded 11-tuple trajectory algorithm each classify all 2048 inputs and agree on 20 fixed configurations, 61 primitive two-cycle orbits, all individual basin populations and entry-time counts. Explicit finite checking establishes \(F^8=F^6\) and a witness for failure of \(F^7=F^5\); a separate full GraphMatcher automorphism enumeration gives 12 symmetries and six versus eleven geometric classes. See embedded check_functional.py and check_trajectory_symmetry.py, both executed successfully. This is a fully exhaustive finite proof, not sample evidence.

value.rationale: Herschel is a natural smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph, not an arbitrary graph slice; a complete finite dynamical classification is a self-contained benchmark. Distinguishing only 142 initially recurrent states from 48 states requiring the sharp sixth update, all of which enter fixed states, and separating individual basin scales and automorphism classes produces information unavailable from general period-at-most-two theorems. Complete classifications and exact natural first-entry and basin invariants have independent mathematical value without claiming an all-graph theorem.
